doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Drummer influences: Philly Joe, Blakey, Clarke, Higgins, Buddy Rich
summary: His biggest drum influences and a Buddy Rich story via Frank DeVito.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Who were your biggest influences in terms of drummers?

Oh man, well Philly Joe really and “Billy Boy” man, you know, listen to that one. What’s wrong with that? “Billy Boy” man. And Art Blakey man, in the very beginning Art Blakey was just thundering. And Kenny Clarke man. Brushes? Kenny Clarke, what a player man. I loved Billy Higgins though too. Billy Higgins. And Buddy. I was on the phone with Frank DeVito last night, my cousin who is a drummer from Utica and he’s like 90 now, 91. We were talking about, every once in a while we talk about Buddy Rich. You have to.

You just have to. And we were talking about Buddy’s — well you know certain things he did man — the feel he got where other people tried doing it in that era and they couldn’t quite do it like he could do it. He was like a magician man. And he never, he never messed up man. He never got hung up on anything, no matter what he tried to play he could play. It was just like a miracle man, to watch it. And Frank, he was pretty good friends with him. And Buddy, he was a character man. And he was over at Frank’s house one day and Frank has got a pair of drumsticks on the coffee table, right? And so Frank says, “Hey Buddy, what is that, what is that you do there?” Buddy picks up the sticks, “What are you talking about?” And you know Buddy was crass. So Frank tells me he picks up the sticks and he starts playing all this shit on the coffee table. It blew his mind. It was just paradiddles [scats]. He was like he just tossed it like it was nothing. And I got a kick out of that story.
